cases.title: Open Graph and Twitter cards describe the same page
cases.why: Open Graph tags are present. A Twitter card tag is present. A later case would assert og:title, og:image, and the card type.

cases.title: Structured data is valid when the page publishes it

cases.title: The h1 and the title agree
cases.why: The first h1 is "CARLOS A. MUÑOZ". The title and the h1 do not have to be identical, and they should not describe different pages.

cases.title: Same-host links discovered from the start page resolve
cases.why: 5 same-host links were listed, 1 of them only after JavaScript ran. This review opened at most 20 of them and did not click them. A later run would request each href and accept only an HTML document on this host.

cases.title: The crawl stays inside the page cap and the host
cases.why: 10 HTML pages were saved, 2 links deep at most, with a cap of 20 pages. A regression would fail if a link left the host or if the cap stopped hiding a broken primary path.

cases.title: A crawler honors robots.txt for linked pages
cases.why: 1 linked URLs were skipped because robots.txt disallows them for this agent. The start URL is still fetched. A later crawler case would log each skipped path.

cases.title: In-page anchors and repeated hrefs stay intentional
cases.why: Same-host hrefs were deduped before the crawl. A UI case would open repeated navigation items once and check that a hash target exists on the page.

cases.title: Visible fields have labels
cases.why: 2 form(s) are present. 0 controls had no label element, aria-label, aria-labelledby, or title. Nothing was submitted. A later case would pair each control with its label.

cases.title: A later functional run uses a test account the owner provides
cases.why: Submitting the form is a different act from reading it. The account, the fixture data, and the expected confirmation stay outside this review.

cases.title: Required fields block an empty submit
cases.why: 5 inputs were marked required in the HTML. A browser case would submit the empty form and expect the constraint message, without creating a record.

cases.title: File inputs state an accepted type before a file is chosen
cases.why: A file input is present. The case would assert the accept attribute and would not upload a file during this proposal.

cases.title: Images expose a text alternative
cases.why: 12 images, 0 without an alt attribute. Informative images need text. Decorative images need an empty alt.

cases.title: The page has a main landmark and a skip link
cases.why: A main element is present. No skip link was found. The review's headless browser runs axe-core on the rendered page.

cases.title: Heading order follows h1 then h2

cases.title: Text contrast and keyboard focus are checked on the rendered page
cases.why: Contrast is measured by axe-core in the review's headless browser. Focus order still needs a person: the case would tab from the top of the page and record the focus ring.

cases.title: HTTPS is the only way in
cases.why: The review refused any URL that was not https on port 443. A browser case would also request the http address and expect a redirect to https.

cases.title: HSTS is set

cases.title: A content security policy is set
cases.why: content-security-policy was absent. The policy would be checked for script-src and frame-ancestors, not only for the header name.

cases.title: nosniff and a frame policy are set
cases.why: x-content-type-options: absent. x-frame-options: absent. A framed copy of the page would be expected to fail when a frame policy is present.

cases.title: Referrer-Policy is set
cases.why: referrer-policy was absent. The later case would open an outbound link and confirm the referrer is no wider than the policy.

cases.title: Response headers do not need to reveal the server build
cases.why: Server header: GitHub.com. The case records the header and does not treat a product name as a vulnerability by itself.

cases.title: A permissions policy limits powerful features

cases.title: The HTML does not reference plain http resources
cases.why: 0 scripts, images, frames, or stylesheets load over plain http. Mixed content would be confirmed in a browser console, not by downloading those URLs here.

cases.why: No privacy or legal wording was found in the markup. Confirm the link in a browser before treating it as found.

cases.title: Third-party scripts are named before they run
cases.why: 2 other hosts were referenced by script src (www.googletagmanager.com, cdnjs.cloudflare.com). A privacy case would load the page with tags blocked and then with consent.

cases.title: AI answer and search crawlers may read the site
cases.why: robots.txt would be read for OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, PerplexityBot, Perplexity-User, Claude-SearchBot, and Claude-User. A full Disallow for any of them keeps the site out of the answers that product writes. Training crawlers are a separate choice and are not asserted here.

cases.why: The case fetches /llms.txt and expects a > summary line, the layout llmstxt.org proposes. It is a convention some AI tools read, not a ranking factor.

cases.title: The main heading and text are in the HTML before scripts run
cases.why: 621 words of text were in the served HTML. Most AI crawlers do not run JavaScript, so they quote only what the server sends.

cases.why: A Person entity is published in JSON-LD. AI answers use the entity to name the brand, its logo, and its profiles.

cases.title: Content pages show when they were published or changed

insights.summary: carlosandmunoz.com scores 86 out of 100 (B). 1 check fails now, 15 are at risk, and 32 pass. Fix first: HSTS is not sent.

findings.title: HSTS is not sent
findings.evidence: strict-transport-security was absent on the start page. Missing on all 10 pages analyzed. A first visit over http can be intercepted.

findings.title: Other sites can frame the page
findings.evidence: Neither X-Frame-Options nor CSP frame-ancestors was sent, so the page can be framed for clickjacking. Missing on all 10 pages analyzed.
findings.fix: Send Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self' (and X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN for old browsers).

findings.title: No content security policy
findings.evidence: content-security-policy was absent on the start page. Missing on all 10 pages analyzed. Injected scripts are not limited by the browser.
findings.fix: Start with the Report-Only policy in the fix kit, watch the reports for a week, then enforce it.

findings.title: X-Content-Type-Options is not sent
findings.evidence: Browsers may guess a file's type and run it as script. Missing on all 10 pages analyzed.

findings.title: Referrer-Policy is not sent
findings.evidence: Browsers fall back to their default. An explicit policy keeps full URLs from leaking to other sites. Missing on all 10 pages analyzed.

findings.title: Permissions-Policy is not sent
findings.evidence: Embedded content can ask for the camera, microphone, or location. Missing on all 10 pages analyzed.

findings.title: 4 scripts block the first paint
findings.evidence: They sit in <head> without async or defer.
findings.fix: Add defer to scripts that do not need to run before the page shows.

findings.title: 10 images have no width or height
findings.evidence: The layout jumps when they load, which hurts Cumulative Layout Shift.
findings.fix: Set width and height (or aspect-ratio) on images.

findings.title: 3 titles run past about 60 characters
findings.evidence: / (77), /?download=pdf (77), /index.html (77). Google cuts them with an ellipsis.
findings.fix: Lead with the words that matter and keep titles near 60 characters.

findings.title: AI crawlers see only part of the text people see
findings.evidence: /?lang=es (24%), /qa-lab.html (18%), /simulador.html (17%). The share is words in the HTML compared with words on the rendered page. Most AI crawlers do not run JavaScript.
findings.fix: Render the main content on the server or pre-render it at build time.

findings.title: No CAA record limits who may issue certificates
findings.evidence: carlosandmunoz.com has no CAA record, so any certificate authority may issue for it.
findings.fix: Add a CAA record for the authority you use, for example 0 issue "letsencrypt.org".

findings.title: 4 indexable pages carry fewer than 150 words in the HTML
findings.evidence: /media/qa-lab-running.html (28 words), /media/qa-lab-tour.html (24 words), /media/sdlc-studio-running.html (22 words), /media/sdlc-studio-tour.html (22 words).
findings.fix: Add useful copy, merge thin pages, or mark them noindex.

findings.title: Pages do not say when they were updated
findings.evidence: Author and date signals help search engines and AI answers judge whether a page is current and credible.
findings.fix: Show an author and a last-updated date on content pages, and add them to the JSON-LD.

findings.title: DMARC only monitors
findings.evidence: The policy is p=none, so spoofed mail is still delivered.
findings.fix: Move to p=quarantine, then p=reject, once reports look clean.

findings.title: Lighthouse scores performance 64/100 on mobile
findings.evidence: Lighthouse 13.5.0 on a simulated mid-range phone over slow 4G: Largest Contentful Paint 8.6 s, Total Blocking Time 98 ms, Cumulative Layout Shift 0.002, Speed Index 4.8 s.
findings.fix: Open PageSpeed Insights for this URL and work through its opportunities, largest savings first.

findings.title: The largest element paints after 2.8 s
findings.evidence: Measured once in Chromium from an EU address (Belgium) with no network throttling. A phone on mobile data will be slower. Good is under 2.5 s.
findings.fix: Preload the hero image and defer scripts that do not affect the first view.

findings.title: Too few Chrome visits for real-user Core Web Vitals
findings.evidence: The Chrome UX Report publishes numbers only after a page or site has enough traffic over 28 days. The Lighthouse lab run below stands in.
